# Requirements Document: Re-accommodation before the seller answers

## Introduction

When the airline moves a customer to other flights, it replaces the affected
order item with a new one, as a paid change does.  In the itinerary change
worked example the replacement is already in the order, at a higher order
version, while the seller's Accept is still pending, and the new services
start CONFIRMED.  The sources do not say whether a change awaiting acceptance
is provisional, so the model takes the answer as a parameter, a reading of the
sources.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/Reaccommodate.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/airline-order-verified/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/AirlineChange/Reaccommodate.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-705

**User Story:** As a customer whose flights the airline changed, I want the new flights in my order at no extra cost and the old ones kept until I accept, so that I can still choose what to do.

**Rule:** WHEN the airline moves a customer to other flights THE SYSTEM SHALL replace the affected order item with a new item at the same price, holding a service for each passenger on each new flight. (Lean: `notifyChange`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHERE an airline change takes effect when it is notified THE SYSTEM SHALL replace the changed order item as a paid change does and raise the order version by one.
   - ONE-705.1, proven: proven theorem `notify_at_notice`; example `itineraryReaccommodated`
2. WHERE an airline change waits for the seller's Accept THE SYSTEM SHALL leave the order and its version unchanged when the change is notified.
   - ONE-705.2, proven: proven theorem `notify_at_acceptance`; example `itineraryReaccommodated`
3. WHEN an airline change takes effect THE SYSTEM SHALL give the new order item the original item's price and a service for each passenger of the original item on each new flight.
   - ONE-705.3, proven: proven theorem `notify_new_item`; example `itineraryReaccommodated`
4. WHILE the seller's Accept of an airline change is pending THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the original order item with the status it had.
   - ONE-705.4, open: open theorem `accept_pending_keeps_original`; counterexample `itineraryReaccommodated`
5. WHEN the airline replaces paid services at no price difference THE SYSTEM SHALL mark every service of the new order item READY TO PROCEED.
   - ONE-705.5, open: open theorem `reaccommodated_paid`; counterexample `itineraryReaccommodated`

#### Open question on ONE-705.4

> While the seller's Accept of an airline change is pending, the original
> order item keeps the status it had.
>
> Open question for the business.  In the itinerary change worked example the
> change is already in the order while Accept is pending: the original item is
> CANCELLED at the next version.  A customer who would rather keep the original
> flights cannot get them back, so Accept offers no real choice.  The example
> `itineraryReaccommodated` shows it under the reading that applies the
> change at notice.  Is a change awaiting acceptance provisional, and does
> declining it restore the original item or only let the customer cancel or
> reshop from the changed order?

#### Open question on ONE-705.5

> When the airline replaces paid services at no price difference, every
> service of the new order item is READY TO PROCEED.
>
> Open question for the business.  In the itinerary change worked example the
> services the airline creates start CONFIRMED, a status the Order concept
> reserves for services still awaiting payment, although the customer paid in
> full and the exchange is even.  If CONFIRMED is read as unpaid, a payment
> time limit could apply to a trip the customer already paid for.  The example
> `itineraryReaccommodated` shows the new services CONFIRMED.  Does the
> paid status carry across an airline change?
